auditedPrs.notes: Squash 8e2de14. Read against tailscale/tailscale @ e2ed432399c9b0fda7aa14e9eb27784d2d893c55 (wgengine/magicsock/magicsock.go handleDiscoMessage, unambiguousNodeKeyOfPingLocked, handlePingLocked, sendDiscoMessage, sendAddr; derp.go processDERPReadResult, derpWriteChanForRegion; endpoint.go discoPing, checkAndUpdateDiscoKey). The core port is right: a naked disco Ping over DERP from a known peer is answered with Pong{TxID, Src: 127.3.3.40:<region>} sealed to the sender's disco key and sent to the DERP source node key on the region it arrived on, nothing is learned, a Geneve-framed ping over DERP goes to the dataplane, an unknown DERP source gets no pong, the inactive-disco-key sighting is forwarded like checkAndUpdateDiscoKey, and the tests decode the production pong. Three minor divergences remain (below): admission is tied to a single disco->node binding where Go allows a set, the DERP-only fallback (no direct socket) still drops the ping, and the pong send is inline and fatal to the region run where Go queues and drops. Adjacent, out of this PR's scope and pre-existing: this tree never sends a disco Ping over DERP (only CallMeMaybe), so a Pong over DERP is still dropped and a local ping over DERP is not offered.

findings.title: DERP ping admission requires a single disco->node binding; Go accepts any known peer for derpNodeSrc
findings.detail: Upstream handlePingLocked over DERP pongs when the sender's disco key belongs to any known peer (handleDiscoMessage: peerMap.knownPeerDiscoKey(sender)) and derpNodeSrc resolves to any peer endpoint (numNodes = 1 if endpointForNodeKey(derpNodeSrc) ok); the disco->node relation is a set (peerMap.nodesOfDisco, 'Multiple nodes may share the same disco key in the case of node sharing and users switching accounts'). Merged answer_derp_ping asks verify(sender_disco, Some(derp_src_node_key)), which in ts_runtime::direct::verify_binding resolves the disco key through PeerDb::peer_by_known_disco_key (a HashMap<DiscoPublicKey, PeerId>, one peer per disco key) and requires that peer's node key to equal the DERP source. When two netmap nodes carry the same disco key (a shared node / one machine under two accounts), only the node that won the index slot gets a pong; the other's `tailscale ping` over DERP times out, the symptom the PR set out to remove. The PR's DECISIONS names only the cross-peer relay case as the deliberately stricter refusal and claims interop is unaffected; the shared-disco-key case is a real peer sealing with its own key. Inherited from the direct arm's verifier shape, but the PR ports the DERP arm onto it.

findings.title: A DERP ping is still dropped, not ponged, when the direct UDP socket is absent
findings.detail: Upstream processDERPReadResult hands every non-Geneve disco frame to handleDiscoMessage and handlePingLocked replies over DERP through sendAddr/derpWriteChanForRegion; no UDP socket is involved and DERP-only operation still answers pings. Merged run_derp_once snapshots direct_sock and demux_relayed_disco only calls handle_relayed_disco when sock is Some; with sock None (bind failure, or the startup window before the direct manager installs it, the tree's documented 'DERP-only' fallback) the ping falls through to the dataplane as junk and no pong is produced. The PR's stated symptom (a Go peer's tailscale ping over DERP timing out against a healthy node) therefore persists in exactly the mode where DERP is the only path. Pre-existing plumbing that the PR did not change, but the ported behaviour is gated on it.

findings.title: Pong over DERP is sent inline in the recv loop and a send error tears down the region run; Go queues and drops
findings.detail: Upstream answers with `go c.sendDiscoMessage(...)` and sendAddr enqueues the frame on the region's derpWriteRequest channel: a full queue drops the packet (metricSendDERPDropped / errDropDerpPacket) and a send error is logged and discarded; the DERP read loop is never blocked and the connection is never torn down for a failed pong. Merged run_derp_once does `client.send_one(to, &frame).await?` for each reply inside the batch loop, so the region's recv loop stalls on the write, and any error ends run_derp_once and reconnects the region (the PR's DECISIONS accepts this as matching the existing queued-disco path, but that path goes through a bounded mpsc with try_send drop semantics, which is the Go shape; the pong bypasses it).
